# Example data: hourly GPS fixes from five elk (SIMULATED)

**These data are simulated. No real elk were collared.** They were generated by the
module's own simulator, so the true parameter values are known. That lets you check
whether the analysis gets the right answer.

## The story

A wildlife biologist collared five adult female Roosevelt elk (*Cervus canadensis
roosevelti*) in the Oregon Coast Range. The collars took one GPS fix per hour for 30
days in June 2024. About 5% of fixes failed, which is common under dense canopy. For
each fix, the biologist extracted the percent forest cover around the location from a
land-cover raster.

The biologist wants to know:

- whether the elk switch between a slow "encamped" mode (bedding, foraging in a patch)
  and a fast "travelling" mode;
- how much of their time they spend in each mode;
- whether switching depends on the time of day and on the forest cover where the elk is.

## Design

| Dimension | Value |
|---|---|
| Animals | 5 (elk_F01 to elk_F05) |
| Fix schedule | 1 fix per hour, nominal |
| Fixes per animal (simulated) | 720 (30 days) |
| Fixes in the file | 3416 (677 to 690 per animal; failed fixes are absent) |
| Failed fixes | 5% at random (184 of 3600 hourly slots after regularising) |
| Fix-time jitter | up to +/- 2 min around the hour |
| Dates | 2024-06-01 to 2024-07-01 (local time, America/Los_Angeles) |
| Area | 20 x 20 km landscape, about -123.56 to -123.05 E, 44.28 to 44.60 N |
| Habitat covariate | percent forest cover at each fix, 10.5 to 88.0 (mean 52.6) |

## Columns of `elk_gps.csv`

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `animal_id` | collar / animal identifier (text) |
| `timestamp` | local date-time of the fix, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, time zone America/Los_Angeles |
| `longitude` | WGS84 decimal degrees (east is positive, so these are negative) |
| `latitude` | WGS84 decimal degrees |
| `forest_cover_pct` | percent forest cover at the fix location (0-100) |

One row per successful fix. Failed fixes are simply missing rows.

## How the data were made

Generator: `dev/movement-hmm/make_example.R`, which calls

    module$simulate(defaults$params, defaults$design + {n_animals: 5, n_fixes: 720,
                    start: "2024-06-01 00:00:00"}, seed = 2024)

The simulator creates correlated random-walk tracks on a smooth forest-cover surface.
The behavioural state switches hourly according to a 2-state Markov chain. Its switching
probabilities depend on the hour of day and on forest cover at the animal's location.
The track is shifted into UTM zone 10N (Oregon Coast Range) and written as lon/lat.
The true values are stored in `example_truth.rds`. `recovery.yaml` holds the same
parameters and design for the planted-truth check.

## TRUE parameter values (simulated)

State 1 = encamped (short steps), state 2 = travelling (long steps).

| Parameter | True value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| step_mean_m_state1 | 60 m | mean hourly step, encamped |
| step_mean_m_state2 | 450 m | mean hourly step, travelling |
| step_sd_m_state1 | 50 m | SD of hourly step, encamped |
| step_sd_m_state2 | 300 m | SD of hourly step, travelling |
| turn_concentration_state1 | 0.5 | von Mises concentration (little directional persistence) |
| turn_concentration_state2 | 2.5 | von Mises concentration (fairly straight travel) |
| tpm_1to2_intercept | -1.667 | log-odds encamped -> travelling vs staying, at this dataset's mean forest (52.6%) and daily-mean hour (-1.6 at 50% forest) |
| tpm_2to1_intercept | -1.133 | log-odds travelling -> encamped vs staying, same reference (-1.2 at 50% forest) |
| tpm_1to2_tod_cos | -0.9 | time-of-day effect, cos(2 pi h / 24) |
| tpm_2to1_tod_cos | 0.7 | |
| tpm_1to2_tod_sin | 0.4 | time-of-day effect, sin(2 pi h / 24) |
| tpm_2to1_tod_sin | -0.3 | |
| tpm_1to2_forest | -0.025 per 1% forest | more forest, less likely to start travelling |
| tpm_2to1_forest | +0.025 per 1% forest | more forest, more likely to stop travelling |
| activity_budget_state1 | 0.586 | long-run share of time encamped (over the daily cycle, at mean forest) |
| activity_budget_state2 | 0.414 | long-run share of time travelling |

The intercepts and the activity budget depend on the reference forest value, so they are
specific to this dataset's mean forest cover. The other values are fixed simulation inputs.
